scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (Acting in a Terrible Way) for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, my brother and I live with our parents. He's 30 and went back to school after being in a bad job, which is why he moved back in about 11 months ago. I'm 21, in my third year of university, working to put myself through school, and studying business. I've been saving money from my paychecks to go on a big vacation after I graduate, probably a cruise or a trip to Japan or Europe. My savings are around $2800 now. My brother hasn't been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. Our parents already help him financially, so he wouldn't ask them for more help. Last week, when he was complaining to our parents about not being able to go on a vacation, they mentioned my vacation fund and suggested that he could start saving now to afford a trip in a year. Three days ago, he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go to Japan this summer or fall. He said since I won't need it for another two years, there's plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about the same as I do, but he always seems broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I don't pay rent either, which is why I've been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone, and uni fees). He's very mad that I said no. He says it's not fair because, as the youngest child, I get to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it's not fair that I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went, whereas he had to go back. He says I've only been able to save so much money because mom and dad spoiled me. I disagree. My father, as well as my university accounting and finance classes, taught me to budget. If anything, I think my parents spoiled him because he doesn't know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don't think it's fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he'll be able to pay me back in time. Even if he could, I'm uncomfortable with the idea. Another point is that our parents are already helping him financially, so he shouldn't be asking me for more help. I'm also contributing financially to my own education and expenses, which is a lot. I'm also concerned about the precedent this sets. If I lend him money now, he might expect me to do it again in the future, which I'm not comfortable with. Plus, if he doesn't pay me back, it could strain our relationship further. I also need to think about my own financial security. If I give him $2800, that's a significant amount of money that I've saved up. I need that for my vacation, and I don't want to jeopardize that. Plus, I don't know if I'll be able to save that amount again if I lend it to him. Another angle is the emotional impact. My brother is upset with me, and that's making me uncomfortable. I don't want to hurt his feelings, but I also don't want to compromise my own goals and financial stability. I also need to consider if there's a middle ground. My brother has poor financial habits and a history of being bad with money. 2. I need to maintain my own financial security and not jeopardize my future plans. Given all these factors, I don't think it's AITA for me to refuse to loan my brother my vacation money.
